- **[Stage]** Google's quality talk said good content can be created for literally any vertical, answering site owners who say they do not know how to become experts or make their content stand out.
  <br><sub>`D3-C192` · Day 3, How Google thinks about Quality (Google)</sub>

- **[Stage]** Google's quality talk showed, as an example of strong content, a running-shoe review site that cut the shoes apart, examined the upper and the foam density under a microscope, took high-quality images, built a test rig and created its own metrics to compare shoes (site not named, slide not photographed).
  <br><sub>`D3-C193` · Day 3, How Google thinks about Quality (Google)</sub>

- **[Stage]** Google's quality talk said the speaker believes content in any vertical can go very far when its creators invest in their own knowledge, effort and expertise.
  <br><sub>`D3-C194` · Day 3, How Google thinks about Quality (Google)</sub>

- **[Docs]** Google's helpful-content guidance says product reviews build trust when readers understand how many products were tested, what the test results were and how the tests were conducted, with evidence of the work such as photographs.
  <br><sub>`D3-C195` · Google Search Central · annotates Day 3, How Google thinks about Quality · is the documentation · [Creating helpful, reliable, people-first content](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/creating-helpful-content)</sub>

- **[Analysis]** For content teams: turn reviews into non-commodity content by testing the products yourselves, publishing your own photos and measurements, explaining the test method and defining comparable metrics across products; a list of common buying tips is the commodity version.
  <br><sub>`D3-C196` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 3, How Google thinks about Quality · [Creating helpful, reliable, people-first content](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/creating-helpful-content)</sub>

- **[Stage]** Google's quality talk said Google discovers tens of billions of spam pages every day.
  <br><sub>`D3-C197` · Day 3, How Google thinks about Quality (Google) · confirmed by Google docs · [Detecting spam to bring you relevant and reliable results](https://www.google.com/search/howsearchworks/how-search-works/detecting-spam/) · Extended by [D3-C239](D3-S07-what-are-quality-updates.md)</sub>

- **[Stage]** Google's quality talk said a big portion of the new pages Google discovers every day is spam, adding that the speaker did not know of Google ever publishing the percentage.
  <br><sub>`D3-C198` · Day 3, How Google thinks about Quality (Google) · not in Google docs</sub>

- **[Stage]** Google's quality talk said spam systems are one of the ways Google protects search quality, removing a very large amount of spam before results are served.
  <br><sub>`D3-C199` · Day 3, How Google thinks about Quality (Google) · confirmed by Google docs · [Detecting spam to bring you relevant and reliable results](https://www.google.com/search/howsearchworks/how-search-works/detecting-spam/), [A guide to Google Search ranking systems](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/ranking-systems-guide)</sub>

- **[Analysis]** The spoken 'tens of billions of spam pages' a day matches Google's How Search Works page, which says its systems find 40 billion spammy pages every day, and the later Day 3 slide '40B spammy pages detected every day' (under 'In 2023'); cite 40 billion a day.
  <br><sub>`D3-C200` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 3, How Google thinks about Quality · [Detecting spam to bring you relevant and reliable results](https://www.google.com/search/howsearchworks/how-search-works/detecting-spam/)</sub>

- **[Stage]** Google's quality talk said Google had released four spam updates in 2026 by the time of the talk on 2 October, with one still rolling out.
  <br><sub>`D3-C201` · Day 3, How Google thinks about Quality (Google) · confirmed by Google docs · [Google Search Status Dashboard](https://status.search.google.com/products/rGHU1u87FJnkP6W2GwMi/history), [Google Search Status Dashboard](https://status.search.google.com/incidents/XhUDXP7A67iHCD2kmbVu)</sub>

- **[Docs]** Google's Search Status Dashboard says the September 2026 spam update began on 24 September 2026, applies globally to all languages and may take up to two weeks to roll out.
  <br><sub>`D3-C202` · Google Search Status Dashboard (Ranking incident history), Google Search Status Dashboard (September 2026 spam update) · annotates Day 3, How Google thinks about Quality · is the documentation · [Google Search Status Dashboard](https://status.search.google.com/products/rGHU1u87FJnkP6W2GwMi/history), [Google Search Status Dashboard](https://status.search.google.com/incidents/XhUDXP7A67iHCD2kmbVu)</sub>

- **[Stage]** Google's quality talk said its spam updates mostly target spam pages, so most site owners in the audience were probably not affected.
  <br><sub>`D3-C203` · Day 3, How Google thinks about Quality (Google) · consistent with Google docs · [Google Search spam updates and your site](https://developers.google.com/search/updates/spam-updates) · Used by the glossary term *Spam update*</sub>

- **[Stage]** Google's quality talk said evaluating the quality of the web at scale is messy and hard, and that Google's work on it is never done.
  <br><sub>`D3-C204` · Day 3, How Google thinks about Quality (Google)</sub>

- **[Stage]** Google's quality talk said AI has fundamentally changed how Google builds spam updates, letting it evaluate many more candidates and drastically increasing its velocity, so it launches faster with more impact.
  <br><sub>`D3-C205` · Day 3, How Google thinks about Quality (Google) · consistent with Google docs · [Detecting spam to bring you relevant and reliable results](https://www.google.com/search/howsearchworks/how-search-works/detecting-spam/), [Google Search spam updates and your site](https://developers.google.com/search/updates/spam-updates) · Extends [D2-C668](D2-S19-calculating-some-signals.md)</sub>

- **[Stage]** Google's quality talk said AI lets Google catch new types of spam and catch more of it.
  <br><sub>`D3-C206` · Day 3, How Google thinks about Quality (Google) · confirmed by Google docs · [Google Search spam updates and your site](https://developers.google.com/search/updates/spam-updates) · Extends [D2-C668](D2-S19-calculating-some-signals.md)</sub>

- **[Stage]** Google's quality talk listed recent updates to Google's spam policies: back button hijacking, scaled content abuse and manipulating AI responses.
  <br><sub>`D3-C207` · Day 3, How Google thinks about Quality (Google) · confirmed by Google docs · [Latest documentation updates](https://developers.google.com/search/updates), [Spam policies for Google web search](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/essentials/spam-policies) · Extended by [D3-C284](D3-S07-what-are-quality-updates.md) · Used by `DEV-SPM-01`, `DEV-SPM-02`</sub>

- **[Stage]** Google's quality talk said back button hijacking was added after many user complaints about pressing the back button and landing on an auto-generated page, or staying on the same site after pressing it twice.
  <br><sub>`D3-C208` · Day 3, How Google thinks about Quality (Google) · consistent with Google docs · [Introducing a new spam policy for "back button hijacking"](https://developers.google.com/search/blog/2026/04/back-button-hijacking), [Spam policies for Google web search](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/essentials/spam-policies) · Used by `DEV-SPM-01`, the glossary term *Back button hijacking*</sub>

- **[Docs]** Google announced on 13 April 2026 that back button hijacking is an explicit violation of its malicious practices spam policy, with enforcement from 15 June 2026; pages that do it may get manual spam actions or automated demotions.
  <br><sub>`D3-C209` · Search Central blog (13 April 2026), Google Search Central · annotates Day 3, How Google thinks about Quality · is the documentation · [Introducing a new spam policy for "back button hijacking"](https://developers.google.com/search/blog/2026/04/back-button-hijacking), [Spam policies for Google web search](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/essentials/spam-policies) · Used by `DEV-SPM-01`, the glossary term *Back button hijacking*</sub>

- **[Docs]** Google's back button hijacking announcement says some instances may come from a site's included libraries or advertising platform, and asks site owners to remove or disable any code, imports or configurations responsible.
  <br><sub>`D3-C210` · Search Central blog (13 April 2026) · annotates Day 3, How Google thinks about Quality · is the documentation · [Introducing a new spam policy for "back button hijacking"](https://developers.google.com/search/blog/2026/04/back-button-hijacking) · Used by `DEV-SPM-01`</sub>

- **[Analysis]** For development teams: test that the browser back button returns users from your pages to where they came from, including search results; audit scripts that call the History API, insert interstitial or 'recommended' pages, or come from ad and engagement vendors.
  <br><sub>`D3-C211` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 3, How Google thinks about Quality · [Introducing a new spam policy for "back button hijacking"](https://developers.google.com/search/blog/2026/04/back-button-hijacking) · Used by `DEV-SPM-01`</sub>

- **[Stage]** Google's quality talk said Google clarified that traditional spam techniques aimed at manipulating AI responses also violate its spam policies, and that Google can take action against them.
  <br><sub>`D3-C212` · Day 3, How Google thinks about Quality (Google) · confirmed by Google docs · [Spam policies for Google web search](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/essentials/spam-policies), [Latest documentation updates](https://developers.google.com/search/updates) · Extends [D1-C129](D1-S03-how-search-works-and-where-s-ai.md)</sub>

- **[Analysis]** Tactics sold as AI visibility or GEO, such as hidden text aimed at AI answers, mass-produced pages for fan-out queries or keyword-stuffed passages, are judged under the same spam policies as classic ranking manipulation.
  <br><sub>`D3-C213` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 3, How Google thinks about Quality · [Spam policies for Google web search](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/essentials/spam-policies) · Used by `DEV-SPM-02`</sub>

- **[Stage]** Google's quality talk said Google reads spam reports and uses them to decide what kinds of spam to tackle next.
  <br><sub>`D3-C214` · Day 3, How Google thinks about Quality (Google) · consistent with Google docs · [Report spam, phishing, or malware](https://developers.google.com/search/help/report-quality-issues), [Spam policies for Google web search](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/essentials/spam-policies)</sub>

- **[Docs]** Since April 2026 Google's spam report page says Google may use a report to take manual action, and that the submission text is sent to the site owner, so reports containing personally identifying information are not processed.
  <br><sub>`D3-C215` · Google Search Central · annotates Day 3, How Google thinks about Quality · is the documentation · [Report spam, phishing, or malware](https://developers.google.com/search/help/report-quality-issues), [Latest documentation updates](https://developers.google.com/search/updates)</sub>

- **[Stage]** Google's quality talk said Google receives a lot of feedback at conferences and online, and invited attendees to share the quality issues they run into or want Google to work on next.
  <br><sub>`D3-C216` · Day 3, How Google thinks about Quality (Google)</sub>

- **[Analysis]** On 1 October 2026, during the event, Google updated its generative AI content guide with rater-guideline material to keep its documentation in sync with its developer-event presentations, and the helpful-content page, updated the same day, carries the effort, originality, talent or skill and accuracy definitions from the quality talk; cite those pages rather than the talk.
  <br><sub>`D3-C217` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 3, How Google thinks about Quality · [Latest documentation updates](https://developers.google.com/search/updates), [Google Search's guidance on using generative AI content on your website](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/using-gen-ai-content), [Creating helpful, reliable, people-first content](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/creating-helpful-content)</sub>
